observation.visible_scene: A beach at sunset/dusk. In the right-center foreground a bonfire burns on the sand, with two dark angled driftwood branches (one pointing up-left, one lying down-right) sticking out of the flame base. Behind the fire is a calm sea meeting a horizon line, under a sky of orange and blue-grey clouds. A red glow from the fire illuminates the sand around the pit. The logs, waterline, horizon, and cloud pattern hold fixed positions across all frames; no camera pan/zoom is evident.
visible_changes: The main flame body continuously flickers, deforms, and changes height/shape frame to frame (tongues elongating vertically, brightening and dimming).

Detached flame wisps/embers appear above the fire and evolve: early frames (t=0-0.08) show two separate pale flame blobs floating above the logs (one higher near center, one lower-left); these shift, merge, thin out, and re-form through the segment.

A single rising flame tongue/puff persists above the logs for much of the clip (t≈0.12-1.60), changing its vertical extent and curling shape (e.g., a rounded puff around t=0.52-0.68, a taller tongue around t=0.32-0.48).
The detached wisps drift slowly upward and sideways relative to the static logs, indicating rising hot gas/embers rather than camera motion.
The red sand glow and the overall sunset color balance remain essentially constant throughout.
outside_clip_unknowns: How the fire was lit and whether it continues to burn or dies after the segment.
Wind speed/direction driving the flame shape changes.
Whether the sky darkens further before or after this window.
uncertain_details: Whether the floating pale blobs are separate burning embers or detached flame tongues (shape suggests flame/ember, not reflection).
Any very slight camera drift is not confirmable because the background stays fixed.
Exact moments of wisp detachment versus re-merging with the main flame.
